decisions: Finite explicit process/thread facade retains original per-process WOW scheduling authority. Host lock/event/death/receive operations stay in existing lifecycle binding; no kernel thread objects or separate task selector.

Function moved before DestroyTask, CurrentTaskLock moved before it, and InsertTask moved to EOF to accommodate ambient gpsi macro bindings. Restore original function order with minimal explicit per-function shared-owner expression or facade binding, preserving all bodies and original logical lines. Verify source-order/macros rather than treating moved text as duplicated algorithms.
Explicit PPROCESSINFO replaces PpiCurrent only. Preserve complemented original TDB lock token and nesting; x86 local pointer carrier is not cross-process identity. Existing lock fixture must remain.

gpsi/gpwtiFirst rebound by preprocessor position for DestroyTask and subsequent SleepTask, then gpsi rebound to ptiOld for DirectedYield. Prefer smallest source-local owner expression in affected functions if it removes ordering coupling without new runtime state. Coordinate facade declarations, preserve single shared event counter.

Original unlink/free/waiter/event decrement and active-owner release retained. Modern event reference/free mapping owns actual handle lifetime. Wake next event-bearing task is notification, not permission to run guest; readiness remains enforced in SleepTask.

CurrentThread parameter replaces PtiCurrent; caller forwards through UserYield/DirectedYield. Keep original wait/receive/death ordering, event accounting and EnterWowCritSect owner. Native host wait must preserve alert/death semantics; fixture doubles are not full kernel equivalence.

Readiness filter prevents selecting a native stack suspended inside a host call even with pending TDB events. Existing scope stack belongs to native call/callback and restores previous frame. Fixture exercises skipping unready higher-priority task without consuming its events.

Idle hook requires ready continuation; otherwise guest callback can enter suspended native frame. Preserve readiness at this separate guest-entry edge; it is not redundant with selecting another task.

WOWEXEC hardware-event self-selection also requires ready continuation. Keep pending wake flag until ready; no artificial IRQ/event injection. Dedicated readiness/hardware combination coverage should accompany future simplification.
Task-locked self-wake must not mark suspended native continuation runnable. Fixture checks selected owner and task lock remain but no task event is fabricated.

Final loop guard requires both selected task and ready top scope after nested callback. Native-return owner sets ready then yields/reacquires before popping; selection alone does not prove native continuation returned.

Explicit currentThread and SleepTask forwarding preserve directed target lookup/priority algorithm. Thread lookup belongs existing lifecycle owner, not ambient Windows TEB. Validate cross-task and obsolete target behavior in directed fixture.
Original remove-and-reinsert priority algorithm retained, including equal-priority tail placement. Do not replace with another task queue or reorder by task IDs.

Full host wait/receive/death/APC/lock facade equivalence and allocation-failure recovery require production-path evidence beyond source fixture. Readiness tests directly toggle frame readiness; lifecycle tests exercise nested scopes, but no fresh end-to-end timing/death proof is claimed. Review event signaling failures and exceptional native return in existing owner without adding blanket recovery.
limits: Readiness scopes are existing native stack ownership, not task IDs.
